fields.sample_size: project description: Vida no Vale in the Jequitinhonha, Mucuri and Sao Mateus basins (92 municipalities; baseline 400,000 people without treated water and 800,000 without sewerage); willingness-to-pay survey of 2,500 households (50% in municipal seats, 50% rural); pilot projects with 170 people trained
fields.effect_estimate: Proposed (design-stage) model for universal water and sanitation access: a regional subsidiary of the state water company (COPASA), a public consortium of the 92 municipalities and the State of Minas Gerais, decentralisation and subsidiarity, public participation and an economic structure combining financial viability and social equity (willingness to pay assessed by contingent valuation); conclusions argue economies of scale and regional technical support. Project description and design rationale, not an outcome evaluation; no effect estimates.
fields.study_design: case study / project design description (governance and institutional model for a regional programme)
fields.section: Full text: Introduction; institutional organisation (consortium and regional subsidiary); economic structure and willingness to pay (2,500 households); pilots; Conclusions 8
fields.exact_location: Introduction; institutional organisation (consortium and regional subsidiary); economic structure and willingness to pay (2,500 households); pilots; Conclusions 8

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a description of the Vida no Vale project design in north-east Minas Gerais (92 municipalities; 400,000 without water, 800,000 without sewerage), read in full text 2026-10-04. A regional subsidiary of the state company and a municipal-state consortium are proposed; a 2,500-household willingness-to-pay survey informed tariffs. Design-stage description by project staff; no outcomes.
pdf_note: Hydrology and Earth System Sciences 12:1075-1085 (2008), about 60,000 characters read
notes: Abstract-level extraction accurate; adds the baseline and survey sample. Authors include the state planning secretariat and utility (project implementers); no outcome data, so it cannot count as evidence of effect.
